title: Sharp Pointwise CATE Inference at the Rare-Endpoint Crossover
banked_reason: Matched all-n,q risk and honest-length orders are sound, but the advertised sharp critical decision problem remains open in oeq:critical-decision; projected paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4.
gap_reasons: The advertised sharp critical decision problem remains open in oeq:critical-decision: no full-class limiting experiment, evaluated v_*(c) or ell_*(c), or attaining sharp decisions are supplied.
paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery rejected a false marks-only Poisson reduction, switched angles while preserving the original class and target, and derived matched all-(n,q) squared-risk and exactly honest connected-length orders with total procedures and full-support same-class converses. Seven cited statements were independently checked against original sources, with source corrections and graph integrity verification; the final math panel passed without findings. The field-grade sharp full-class critical experiment and evaluated optimal decision values remain open, so two independent validity checks confirmed a subfield downgrade; no F stages or Lean certification were performed.
tldr: At the rare-endpoint crossover \(q=cn^{-1/4}\), sharp point-CATE risk and honest connected-interval length require a decision theorem beyond an occupied rate diagram. The causal class maintains a public prospective risk envelope and exact known scalar uniform design. A total pair estimator retains endpoint and treatment-neighbor variance, while a legal fine-scale propensity--baseline oscillation has nonvanishing causal centering on the critical scale. The open question derives the complete original-record critical experiment and certified sharp decision values, determining whether this interaction changes Gaussian optimal-inference values after all treatment information is used. A nuisance-fixed localized boundary reduces to a specified Gaussian convex-regression experiment. Neither a statistic normal approximation nor its covariance-centering diagnostic establishes a full-class decision gap.
gap: \cite{kennedy2024minimaxcate} supplies fixed-scale point-CATE rate architecture. \cite{armstrong2018optimalinference} supplies Gaussian convex-regression optimal inference under a linear signal and known covariance. These results do not supply sharp all-procedure critical values for the maintained public rare-risk class with unknown rough confounding and connected worst-case interval length.
fill: The first departure from a Gaussian linear-functional proof is to expand and mix the complete four-mark likelihood with its treatment marginal and propensity--baseline cross-products before imposing a linear-signal reduction. The critical decision question must derive the retained information and evaluate its effect on optimal risk or connected length. The explicit Gaussian boundary calibrates the comparison; a full-class Gaussian reduction, if valid, must be proved. Field positioning rests on the resulting sharp causal decision theorem, not on a presupposed non-Gaussian feature.
